neighbours.label: Reference numbers inside bracketed or parenthesized citations in scientific prose ([7, 8], (24-26)), vs the same sentences with quantities instead of citations
fire: Obesity is linked to a higher risk of several cancers [12, 13].
Similar results have been reported in children and adults (31-33).
Sleep loss impairs memory consolidation in healthy volunteers [5, 6].
The method has been validated in several cohorts (18-21).
Air pollution increases hospital admissions for asthma [22, 23].
This pattern has been observed in many bird species (41-44).
Regular exercise lowers blood pressure in older adults [9, 10].
The protein is overexpressed in most breast tumors (27-29).
quiet: Obesity affects about 12 or 13 percent of adults in the region.
Between 31 and 33 children joined the study each year.
Sleep loss was measured in 5 or 6 healthy volunteers per night.
The method was tested in 18 to 21 patients per clinic.
Air pollution sent 22 or 23 people to the hospital that week.
The team observed 41 to 44 bird species near the lake.
Regular exercise for 9 or 10 hours a week lowers blood pressure.
The protein was found in 27 to 29 of the tumor samples.

predictions: Fire 0.2-0.3 on the separator or digits of a citation list; near misses with numbers as quantities under 0.05. Patent reference numerals ('beams 31 and 32') scored 0.031, so they are not used.
notes: Card: digits and ' [' in numbered lists, citations and patent numerals. Probe: '(24-26)' 0.273 on '-', '[7, 8]' 0.214 on ','; 'beams 31 and 32' 0.031, numbered list '35.' 0.012; quantities '35 dollars' 0.002, '31 cousins' 0.006.
